The Bhola cyclone struck East Pakistan, now Bangladesh, and India's West Bengal on 12 November 1970. It is the deadliest tropical cyclone on record: at least 300,000 people died, perhaps as many as 500,000, most of them drowned when the storm surge flooded the low islands of the Ganges Delta.

The government of Yahya Khan, far away in West Pakistan, was slow and weak in its relief. Many Bengalis took this as proof that the state did not care about them. A month later, in the general election, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and his Awami League won almost every seat in East Pakistan and a majority in the national assembly. The army refused to hand over power, and within months came the Bangladesh Liberation War.

Later Bangladesh built cyclone shelters and warning systems, and storms of similar strength now kill far fewer people.
